# [TASK] Add audit-check.py to verify the mechanical parts of the standard

## Task
Add `infrastructure/scripts/audit-check.py`, which checks issues against the
mechanical parts of the backlog standard.

The standard in `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/audit-artifacts/` is mostly
prose a person has to judge. These parts are not, so re-reading them by hand
on every audit wastes the auditor's attention and misses things:

- exactly one type label, exactly one priority label, an assignee
- no retired `sprint-N` label
- no `## Child Stories`, `## Technical Tasks` or `Parent: #N` line
- a parent link, or a `## No parent` section stating why not
- the template's sections all present
- no acceptance criterion closing on a date instead of a proof
- no closed issue with an unchecked criterion or an open child

It found 24 problems across #251's own subtree on its first run, including
#255 closed with all 6 criteria unchecked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `audit-check.py <n> --tree` reports problems for an issue and
      everything under it, `--all` for the board, `--quiet` for counts
- [ ] It exits non-zero when it finds a problem, so it can gate a run
      (`audit-check.py 252; echo $?` returns 1)
- [ ] Every check maps to a rule stated in `AGENTS.md` or the skill, with
      no rule invented in the script
- [ ] The docstring states what it cannot check: whether a claim is true,
      whether a named test proves anything, and whether the prose reads well
      (`head -20 infrastructure/scripts/audit-check.py`)
- [ ] Running it on #251 --tree reports 0 problems once this audit is done
      (`audit-check.py 251 --tree`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 3

## Notes
This is what makes the audit backlog's own criteria provable. An audit
issue's criteria are inspection statements with no code behind them, so
before this script they could only be confirmed by re-reading. Now the
mechanical half is a command.
